### 1 — Scene
A cooked breakfast-style meal: scrambled eggs, browned Brussels sprouts, and shredded hash-brown potatoes.

### 2 — Vessel
A large, roughly square dinner plate, partly cropped. I’ll use a **26 cm equivalent diameter** for the area calculation:  
3.14 × 13² ≈ **530 cm²**.

### 3 — Items
- Scrambled eggs
- Roasted or pan-fried Brussels sprouts
- Shredded hash browns

Cooking fat appears incorporated into the browned foods; it is included in their energy densities rather than counted separately.

### 4–7 — Area, volume, weight, and energy
Heights are average pile heights, not the tallest points.

| Item | Plate area covered | Area | Height | Gross volume | Bulk density | Weight | kcal/100 g | Energy |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Scrambled eggs | 30% | 159 cm² | 1.4 cm | 223 ml | 0.95 g/ml | 212 g | 160 | 339 kcal |
| Brussels sprouts | 17% | 90 cm² | 2.2 cm | 198 ml | 0.60 g/ml | 119 g | 70 | 83 kcal |
| Hash browns | 20% | 106 cm² | 1.5 cm | 159 ml | 0.65 g/ml | 103 g | 200 | 206 kcal |

Coverage totals **67%**, leaving approximately one-third of the plate bare.

### 8 — Sanity check
Approximately **434 g and 628 kcal** is plausible for the visible large egg portion, several Brussels sprouts, and a moderate pile of hash browns. Plate cropping and the unknown cooking-fat quantity introduce uncertainty.
